title: Canary Output Contract Monitoring Harness (function-call + JSON shape smoke checks)
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Build a lightweight, extensible harness that runs during canary/A-B/shadow rollouts to assert structured-output compatibility and function-call contract stability. The harness will run a mix of deterministic schema validators and stochastic function-call diff checks against production-like samples to surface regressions early and trigger configured rollback policies if thresholds are breached. Goal: reduce undetected schema regressions during model rollouts that cause downstream runtime errors and customer-visible failures.
plan: Phase 1: Spec & quick prototype (2 sprint points) - define contract checks (JSON schema, allowed extra keys, required fields, types), function-call signature diffing rules, and sampling rules for shadow traffic.

Phase 2: Harness implementation (4 points) - implement validator library, lightweight diff engine that computes structured divergences (missing fields, type changes, new function names), and a streaming reporter that emits metrics and traces per invocation.

Phase 3: Integration (6 points) - wire harness into rollout controller: canary + A/B routes and shadow tap; add auto-rollback hooks for configurable thresholds; add UI surface for per-rollout diagnostics.
Phase 4: Eval & safeguards (2 points) - automated regression tests, run in staging with real traffic replay, add rate-limiting / sampling knobs to avoid cost blowup.
Phase 5: Launch & docs (1 point) - rollout to runtime-2.6, runbook for SRE, docs for customers to author compatibility rules.
acceptance_criteria: Canaries record per-invocation schema validation results (pass/fail) and counts of each failure class in metrics (Prometheus) and traces (Jaeger).
Function-call diffs are produced for mismatches: missing args, extra args, arg type changes, and new function names — with example sample payloads attached to the trace.
Rollout controller can be configured with threshold rules (e.g., >1% schema failures or any critical missing-field -> pause and auto-rollback).
Shadow traffic path runs validators without affecting production responses and returns a digest to the harness.
End-to-end test harness simulating staged deployment demonstrates rollback on injected schema change within staging environment.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Running per-invocation validators at full QPS increases CPU cost and latency. Mitigation: default sampling (1%), prefix/KV cache bypass for identical requests, and offload heavy checks to asynchronous evaluator.
Risk: False positives due to optional fields or unstable keys. Mitigation: allow 'fuzzy' rules and allow-list for tolerated differences; provide dry-run mode for rule tuning.
Risk: Overly aggressive auto-rollback could cause churn. Mitigation: require multi-interval confirmation and annealing window before auto-rollback; support manual override.
qa_plan: Unit tests for schema validator and diff engine with 100% branch coverage for core logic.
Integration tests: replay recorded production traces through harness in CI (staging mode).
Chaos test: introduce random extra fields / missing args into staged model to confirm detection and rollback.
implementation_notes: Prefer jsonschema (BSD) for base validation, but wrap to add lightweight path-based suppression rules used by product-owned compatibility lists.
Diff engine returns compact vector of signals: [MISSING_FIELDS, TYPE_CHANGES, NEW_FUNCTIONS, EXTRA_KEYS] with counts and sample payloads (max 5 samples).
Expose a stable API contract for customers to upload their expected JSON schema and function signatures (s3-backed config per project).
